Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. - One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)

Model-facing tool replies must be concise purpose-specific text; keep structured envelopes and internal metadata out of model context. Select only evidence useful to the current question, and expand from index to context to relevant details only as needed.
Use claude-mem for your own durable notes. For local-worker notes, when its save_memory tool is available, save_memory({text, title, project}) records preferences, corrections, decisions, and reusable lessons. For server notes, use observation_add for the selected server project when available; save_memory is local-worker only. Worker runtime: use Smart search by default: follow the mem-search skill in three steps—search({query, project}) for an index, timeline({anchor}) for context around relevant results, then get_observations({ids}) for only the records you choose after reviewing the index and context. Do not use auto or guided modes. Optional Dumb search, dumb_search({query, project}): Doesn’t reason about the results. Fast, but shallow. Use Smart for reliable recall. A hosted read-only connector may expose searches without write tools; do not call a missing write tool.
When connected through CMEM Pro, Smart search uses memory_search({query}), timeline({anchorId}) for context, then selected get_observations({ids}) or get_summaries({ids}). A direct self-hosted /v1/mcp connection uses search({projectId, query}), timeline({projectId, anchorId}), then get_observations({projectId, ids}). Use only tools and argument names advertised by the active connection; no auto or guided modes.
Use work_state_write for to-do lists and changing work state when available. Keep durable notes concise, distinguish verified facts from guesses, and exclude credentials and private material the user asked you not to remember. Native memory files can remain enabled; an explicitly configured memory folder watcher imports their Markdown notes into claude-mem. Never assume a hosted memory search was intercepted: search claude-mem directly when its result is needed.

# Nexus Code v1.1.4 Plan

**Status:** Plan and owner decisions recorded (section 6); execution starts when this PR merges. **Base:** `main` at v1.1.3 (published 2026-11-05, `46fd5045`).
**Scope (owner, 2026-11-04):** (1) resolve every open finding from the v1.1.2 source (shipped as v1.1.3); (2) add Worktrunk functionality in the best-integrated way.

## 1. Principles

- Close findings with the fix first, the regression test red first, and an independent review per work package. Findings are closed with evidence, never by editing the finding.
- No new runtime dependency (gate G1.1-5: zero deprecated packages, `cargo deny`, SBOM, notices). Anything Worktrunk-shaped must be built on Node, git and the system `cp`.
- Project-supplied commands are untrusted input. Nothing a repository file declares runs without an approval that lives outside the repository.
- One exact-head gate per release candidate, run with the CI fixture variables set so `make test` runs through, in a clean worktree with its own `npm ci`.

## 2. Findings ledger

**Numbering.** `WP-1301` to `WP-1308` and `WP-1310` to `WP-1315` below are the v1.1.4 work packages. They supersede the same IDs in `docs/v1.1.0/ROADMAP.md` (OTLP exporter, provenance graph, macOS builds, knowledge freshness, cgroup limits, Composio mesh), which were never scheduled. Those roadmap items keep their own IDs only inside that document; in commits, claims and findings, `WP-13xx` means this plan. If one of them is scheduled later, give it a new ID.

Sources: my independent reviews on PR #402 (WP-1105 evaluators, WP-1107 provider work), Entire trail 145 (15 open findings after the `--step` HIGH was fixed in v1.1.2), Entire trail 140, Entire trail 146, the gate-3 flake recorded in the findings ledger, and the known limitations in `docs/releases/v1.1.2.md` and `docs/releases/v1.1.3.md`. Every item below must end as FIXED (with a test), WITHDRAWN (with evidence it is not a defect) or DEFERRED (owner decision, with a reason). Work packages are ordered by risk.

### WP-1301 Single-step mode and the TUI (WP-1106)
- TUI `/step` calls `agent.runTurn` directly: no rollback checkpoint, no live tool events, no saved session, a blocked turn reported as success. Dispatch it as a normal sidecar job, `runJob(id, undefined, (signal) => this.turn(...))` as the other turn commands do (`cli/src/sidecar.ts:323`, `:353`, `:454`; the runner is `turn()` at `sidecar.ts:557`), so it gets the checkpoint, observer, saved session and `turn.result`. The REPL `/step` already uses `InteractiveRepl.prepareTurnCheckpoint` and `runInteractiveTurn` (`cli/src/repl.ts:196`, `:212`, `:874-875`), which are private to the REPL and are not what the TUI should call.
- `/step` is not `cancellable`.
- The step pause overwrites a `STAGNATION_DETECTED` stop and skips `endStep()`; guard on `!stopReason` and call `endStep()` before pausing, so stagnation detection advances across `/step` calls.
- Tests: drive the real REPL `/step` handler and the TUI `stepSlash`; the current REPL test re-implements the logic and would pass if the handler were deleted.

### WP-1302 Code evaluators (WP-1105)
- **Fail-open overlay (HIGH in review):** build and `typecheck_clean` overlay only `.ts .mts .cts .tsx .js .mjs .cjs .jsx .rs .py` candidate files on the baseline. Carry every candidate build input (additions and deletions), or fail closed and report ignored changed paths.
- Shadowing through `node_modules` and in-repo build helpers (`build.rs`, `setup.py`, `conftest.py`, `tools/*.js`) that are overlaid as source.
- Two full workspace snapshots refuse large `node_modules` (5 s deadline, 50,000 entries).
- Evaluator commands have no memory, pid or disk limits; parsers have no timeout (65 MB `.ts` blocked 62.9 s); a command path that resolves outside the workspace through a symlink or `..`.
- `typecheck_clean`: coded diagnostics only (document or make the recogniser task-supplied); line-shift false failures; identical recognised config errors (TS5057) pass; `--pretty` output.
- `node --check` accepts an ESM-syntax `.js` file that contains a syntax error.
- `diff_boundary` counts evaluator-staged hidden tests as agent changes for non-hardened tasks with `hidden.dir` (run evaluators before staging, or snapshot separately).
- Candidate edits to build configuration are silently ignored: report them.
- Dangling-symlink overlay fails closed with `EEXIST`; pinned workspace under `os.tmpdir()`; `spec.candidate.cwd` overridden; README stale.

### WP-1302b Tool-call syntax counting (`cli/src/parser.ts`)
Split out of WP-1302 because these items edit `cli/src/parser.ts`, not `eval/`. **Owner: claude-code** (decision 3 gives `eval/` to codex-root and does not cover `cli/`); the `eval/evaluators/code/json_repair_rate.mjs` rows in FINDINGS stay with WP-1302.
- `toolCallSyntax` does not count legacy text-mode calls (`NEXUS_TEXT_TOOL_PARSING=legacy` code-block and balanced-object paths never call `count`).
- Native calls whose `function.arguments` is Markdown-fenced JSON are counted as `native`; classify fence removal as a repair before counting.
- Correct the `ToolCallSyntaxCounts` doc and the README to match what is counted.
- Tests drive `parseToolCalls` for each syntax and assert `evaluateJsonRepairRate` output, so an evaluator change cannot hide a counting regression.

### WP-1303 Provider handling (WP-1107)
- `serverKindCache`: add a TTL, invalidate on endpoint, provider and account switch, key by more than the endpoint string. Fix the gateway-on-404 case that sends `X-Task-Class` to a replaced non-gateway server (REQ-PRV-109 must hold for every path, not only the success path).
- Normalise nullable optional arguments once, at parse, for repaired and text-mode calls too; keep an explicit `null` where the schema allows null; remove the duplicate layer.
- A retained vLLM kind keeps `advertised.via` so request counting does not turn off; transient `/version` and Ollama `/api/version` failures must not downgrade a known kind.
- Matrix provenance: bind the archive to the verified checkout content, not only to the commit id.
- Decide the GBNF compiler: wire it to a consumer (llama.cpp `grammar`, vLLM `guided_json`, Ollama `format`) or remove the dead code. Hybrid reasoning grammars from the v1.1.0 roadmap are still unimplemented.
- **Measure G1.1-4** (at least 99.5% valid tool-call JSON across supported provider endpoints) against live endpoints; this needs the shared `GATEWAY` claim. Until measured it stays "not met".
- Test gaps: 404 and thrown-exception kind retention, `agent_observer` isolation of the two normaliser layers, required-null rejection.

### WP-1304 Evaluation CLI, tracing and redaction hygiene
- `--isolated-home` is honoured only when `eval` is `argv[0]`; parse after options or reject the flag when it is not applied (currently silently uses the real HOME).
- `core-v1/tasks/*` duplicates `eval/tasks/*`, and the evaluator runtime file list exists in two places that already differ.
- OTLP scope version is hard-coded `1.1.0`; use `getBuildIdentity().version`.
- Sidecar text is redacted per field and again per event (paths corrupted, special case for `session.state`); choose one layer. Four identical diagnostic helpers (`formatCliDiagnostic`, `formatReplDiagnostic`, `formatProviderDiagnostic`, `formatUpgradeDiagnostic`) and `formatSafeSidecarText`: one shared helper next to `redactDiagnosticForOutput`; the REPL step error path skips redaction.
- Secret-shaped directory names still appear verbatim in `workspace` and `workspace_name` (known nit).

### WP-1305 Release hygiene
- Make the CI fixture variables part of the documented local `make test` invocation (or a `make test-ci` target) so a local gate runs through; make `make test` run the terminal-scope and security steps even when the CLI suite fails, or document the abort.

# Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:

- a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
- full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
- `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
- HEAD moved during a pause.

They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.

## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent

- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
- An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
- An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.

## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)

Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

```sh
CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

| File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
| `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
| `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
| `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/config.ts`, `security.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `plugins.ts` | 01, 03 | Claim required. PLAN-01 PR-1e and PLAN-03 must not run at the same time on `sandbox.ts` or `security.ts`. |
| `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts` | 01, 02 | **PLAN-01 PR-1a (effect classes) lands first.** PLAN-02 PR-2c adds schema fields afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tester.ts` | 01, 11 | **PLAN-01 PR-1c lands before PLAN-11 PR-11b/11c.** |
| `cli/src/core/state.ts` | 04, 08 | **PLAN-08 PR-8a (HOME isolation) lands before everything.** |
| `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs` | 01, 02, 06 | Claim required. The protocol version number is owned by PLAN-02 PR-2a. PLAN-06 PR-6c only reads it. |
| `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{live_state,live_view}.rs` | 01, 02 | Claim required |
| `package.json`, `cli/package.json`, `core/Cargo.toml`, lockfiles | 01, 06, 07, 08 | **Only one agent at a time.** Version fields are written only by `scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Dependency changes are separate commits that touch only the lockfile and manifest. |
| `harness.sh`, `install.sh`, `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `.github/workflows/*` | 05, 06, 07, 09, C1 | Claim required. Workflow edits are separate commits. |
| `cli/dist/**` | all, while tracked | Do not commit `cli/dist` from slices. PLAN-07 PR-7d untracks it (DEC-10). Until that merges, only the merging agent rebuilds and commits dist, in a final separate commit, after rebasing. |
| `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md`, `quickstart.md` | 05, 09 and doc tasks in every plan | Edit only the sections your slice changes. Hold a short `FILE_` claim. |

### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Run a command with the evaluator fixtures that .github/workflows/ci.yml provisions:
+#   NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT  a dedicated 128m tmpfs (mode 0711, owned by the caller)
+#   NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_RUNTIME_ROOT    a public runtime directory (mode 0711, owned by the caller)
+# Same paths, size and modes as CI. The tmpfs and directories are removed when the command ends,
+# but only if this script created them; anything that already exists is refused, never reused or deleted.
+# Usage: scripts/with-ci-fixtures.sh [--check] -- <command> [args...]
+set -euo pipefail
+
+readonly WORKSPACE_ROOT=/mnt/nexus-eval-ci
+readonly RUNTIME_ROOT=/opt/nexus-eval-ci-runtime
+
+check_only=0
+if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then check_only=1; shift; fi
+if [[ "${1:-}" == "--" ]]; then shift; fi
+if [[ $check_only -eq 0 && $# -eq 0 ]]; then
+  echo "usage: $0 [--check] -- <command> [args...]" >&2
+  exit 64
+fi
+
+if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Linux" ]]; then echo "with-ci-fixtures: Linux only (tmpfs mount)" >&2; exit 2; fi
+if [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]]; then echo "with-ci-fixtures: run as the unprivileged user that runs the tests" >&2; exit 2; fi
+if mountpoint -q "$WORKSPACE_ROOT" 2>/dev/null; then
+  echo "with-ci-fixtures: $WORKSPACE_ROOT is already a mount point; refusing to reuse or unmount it" >&2; exit 2
+fi
+for dir in "$WORKSPACE_ROOT" "$RUNTIME_ROOT"; do
+  if [[ -e "$dir" ]]; then
+    echo "with-ci-fixtures: $dir already exists; remove it (when empty) and retry" >&2; exit 2
+  fi
+done
+if [[ $check_only -eq 1 ]]; then
+  echo "with-ci-fixtures: would mount a 128m tmpfs at $WORKSPACE_ROOT and create $RUNTIME_ROOT (needs sudo)"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+mounted=0; created_workspace=0; created_runtime=0
+cleanup() {
+  local status=$?
+  if [[ $mounted -eq 1 ]]; then sudo umount "$WORKSPACE_ROOT" || echo "with-ci-fixtures: could not unmount $WORKSPACE_ROOT" >&2; fi
+  if [[ $created_workspace -eq 1 ]]; then sudo rmdir "$WORKSPACE_ROOT" || true; fi
+  if [[ $created_runtime -eq 1 ]]; then sudo rm -rf --one-file-system -- "$RUNTIME_ROOT"; fi
+  exit "$status"
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+sudo install -d -o "$(id -un)" -g "$(id -gn)" -m 0711 "$WORKSPACE_ROOT"; created_workspace=1
+sudo mount -t tmpfs -o "size=128m,mode=0711,uid=$(id -u),gid=$(id -g)" nexus-eval-ci "$WORKSPACE_ROOT"; mounted=1
+sudo install -d -o "$(id -un)" -g "$(id -gn)" -m 0711 "$RUNTIME_ROOT"; created_runtime=1
+
+NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT="$WORKSPACE_ROOT" NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_RUNTIME_ROOT="$RUNTIME_ROOT" "$@"

- `worktrunk_copy.test.ts` 8/8 and `worktrunk_core.test.ts` pass at this stack (29/29 at #446 head with merge tests). Red commit `f7f8c307` fails at import only (`Cannot find module .../copy.js`): the file is red, but none of the 8 behaviours is individually shown red.

- No new failures in the related suites at head vs base (see my #442 comment).

### Findings
1. **Source-swap race is real and acknowledged, not mitigated** (`copy.ts:84-105` plans with `lstat`; `copy.ts:150` copies later with `copyFileSync`, which follows a link). The default source is the main checkout, where the agent works, and the walk of a large include set (up to 50,000 files) is a long window; a file replaced by a link to `~/.ssh/...` in an ignored directory is copied into the new worktree. The header comment calls the source "the operator's own checkout", but that is the tree the agent edits. Open the source with `O_NOFOLLOW`, `fstat` it (regular file, same dev/ino as planned) and copy from the descriptor, or re-`lstat` immediately before the copy. Same for `copy.ts:147-148`.
2. **Partial copy on error.** `mkdirVerified` or `copyFileSync` throwing mid-loop (`copy.ts:137-153`) leaves a partial tree; `switch -c` turns it into a warning. Acceptable, but say "partially copied" and the count in the warning (`command.ts:99-101`).
3. **Exclusions are top-level only** (`copy.ts:35`, `:116`): a nested `.git`, `.nexus` or `.entire` below an included directory (for example `vendor/x/.git`, `node_modules/*/.git`) is copied. The plan says "exclude `.git`, `.nexus`, `.entire`" without qualification.
4. Low: `--all-ignored` on an automatic `switch -c` is unreachable (good); but `switch -c` copies with no confirmation and no output when `.worktreeinclude` is absent, so a repository-supplied `.worktreeinclude` listing an ignored secret path silently copies it into every new worktree. Within the repo, so no boundary is crossed; just document it.

Everything else in the delta (symlink destinations, caps before writing, virtualenv rule, read-only dry-run) behaved as claimed. Finding 1 should be fixed here or deferred explicitly; the rest are follow-ups.

## Independent review of #446 (WP-1312, delta vs #445 head): REQUEST CHANGES

Head reviewed: `386303d8d43eca0b1430610b0ec1f373821be6b1` (delta `92ad501f..386303d8`: `merge.ts`, `worktrunk_merge.test.ts`, `command.ts`, docs).

### Evidence
- `worktrunk_merge.test.ts` 9/9; combined `worktrunk_core + copy + merge` 29/29 at head. Red commit `306d99a7`: 9/9 fail with `unknown subcommand 'merge'/'prune'` (verified, red for the stated reason).
- The acceptance test (`worktrunk_merge.test.ts:222`) does run create, automatic copy-ignored, `copy-ignored --force`, list --json, merge, prune and remove against a real `mkdtemp` repo; dirty-refusal, escape refusal, hooks and read-only are covered by separate tests rather than in that one flow, which is acceptable for plan section 5.
- Related suites head vs base: no new failures (see #442 comment).
- `prune --dry-run` against this repository (read-only, real home): 0.9 s, kept locked and unmerged worktrees, "86 younger than the minimum age"; nothing removed.
- Probes: rebase conflict left open and target untouched (also tested); detached main checkout -> clear refusal; `remove --force` alone on an unmerged branch is refused, `--delete-unmerged` alone on a dirty tree is refused, both together delete (matches the plan).

### Findings
1. **Not every Git call is pinned: `merge` without `-m` executes repo-local `core.fsmonitor`.** `merge.ts:88` calls `generateConventionalCommit` (`cli/src/git.ts:95-101`), which runs `execSync("git status --porcelain")` through a shell with no `-c core.fsmonitor=false`/`core.hooksPath`. Probe: `.git/config` `core.fsmonitor = "echo FSMONITOR >> marker; exit 0"`; `nexus worktree merge` (dirty worktree, no `-m`) wrote the marker, while the same config did not fire on `list`/`switch` (pinned). Pass the pinned helper's output to the message builder (or make the generator take a status string), and add a test with a marker-writing fsmonitor and `core.hooksPath` hook for the `merge` and `prune` paths. The docs (`WORKTREES.md` Safety) and PR body say all Git calls are pinned.
2. **Half-applied state when the squash commit fails.** `merge.ts:98-99`: `reset --soft <mergeBase>` then `commit`. Probe (`commit.gpgsign=true`, `gpg.program=/bin/false`): the command fails with `git commit failed: error: gpg failed to sign the data:`; the branch now points at the merge base with all changes staged, and the message does not mention `refs/nexus-backup/<branch>`. The PR body lists signing as "could not verify". Restore the original HEAD (`reset --soft <orig>`) on failure, or at minimum print the backup ref and the restore command. The same applies to the later `--no-rebase` ff failure (`merge.ts:119-121`) after the branch was already squashed.
3. **Ambiguous target ref.** `merge.ts:75`, `:118` and prune's `resolveCommit` (`:151`) resolve bare branch names, so a tag with the target's name wins (see #442 finding 4); `merge --ff-only branch` (`:118`) should use `refs/heads/<branch>`.
4. **`merge` deletes ignored files without opt-in, `prune` requires `--discard-ignored`.** `merge.ts:126` calls `removeOne(..., { force: true })`, so `.env`-style ignored files, local notes and caches in the worktree are destroyed after the merge; the doc says only "ignored leftovers (build caches)". Probe: ignored `secret.env` removed silently. Also `git add -A` (`:89`) commits untracked non-ignored files (probe: `.env.local` landed on `main`); this is the plan's behaviour but a warning/listing of swept-in untracked paths would help. Plan 3.3 item 4 (safe removal covers ignored files) argues for the same rule as `prune`.
5. **In-session `/worktree merge` is not the new merge.** `workspace_commands.ts` (+7) and `repl.ts` route `status|merge|discard` to the legacy speculative-worktree handlers, so the named-worktree `merge` is CLI-only; the catalog usage string `catalog.ts:109` lists `merge` twice and `docs/WORKTREES.md` (Commands/Merge sections) reads as if `/worktree merge` works. Document it, or name the in-session form differently.
6. **Prune details.** (a) `merge.ts:190` runs `git worktree prune` for all stale registrations regardless of `--min-age`/`--limit` (a worktree on an unmounted drive loses its metadata); `--dry-run` correctly skips it. (b) The age guard uses the directory's own mtime (`merge.ts:170`), which does not change when files below the top level are edited; it is effectively the HEAD commit time for a clean tree, so a clean, same-commit worktree a user created yesterday for a task not yet started is pruned with its branch after 1 day. That matches `wt` semantics but should be stated in the docs. (c) `removeOne(..., { force: dirty.ignored > 0 })` (`:182`) skips the re-check of tracked changes between `statusOf` and removal for that case.
7. Low: after a successful merge the command removes the worktree that may be the harness's or the shell's cwd (`merge.ts:126`); the validation-receipt gate (CAND-001..004) and LLM commit messages are not implemented (disclosed in the PR and FINDINGS row WP-1312, so the row should say PARTIAL rather than FIXED if the plan item is considered in scope).

### Plan section 5 check
- dirty worktree refuses removal: yes; path escape refused: yes; Git hooks do not run during creation/merge: yes except finding 1 (fsmonitor, a config-driven exec rather than a hook); read-only mode refuses every mutating subcommand: yes through `runWorktreeCommand` and both slash gates, but not for `nexus --read-only worktree ...` (#442 finding 2). Hook approval items belong to WP-1313.

Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES for 1 (contradicts the pinned-git claim and is an exec path) and 2 (state left half-applied without guidance); 3-6 should be fixed or deferred with an owner decision.
